title: The hard part is the next morning
about: This film is the manual's opening. It makes an argument and records nothing; the code it shows is read from examples/plugged-in.

lines.text: An agent can write a working system in an afternoon.
The server. The database. The command line. The tools for other agents. The page of docs.
Writing it was never the hard part.
The hard part is the next morning.
Is it right? Is it fast enough? What happens when something fails?
And when one rule changes, what else has to change?
To answer any of that, someone has to read all of it. Usually, that someone is you.
Orthograph moves the part you read.
You work on the system itself: the things in it, who may do what to them, and what must always be true.
That description is the blueprint. It is small enough to read whole.
Everything below it is made by the framework, or written by an agent inside a frame the blueprint sets.
And nobody takes anyone's word that it works. The running system is proved, against stories you agreed to before it was built.
So three parties do three different jobs.
You decide the system, and you read the blueprint and the stories.
Your agents plan with you, write the stories, build the behaviour, and review each other.
The framework makes the server, the A P I, the S D K and the command line, and proves them.

lines.text: This manual follows one small app, Plugged In. A person claims a name, and gets a public page of links.
Eleven chapters, in the order things happen. Before any code. Build it. Run it. Live with it.
Everything a chapter prints was recorded from a real run. And where something doesn't exist yet, the chapter says so.
Four chapters are written so far. We start where every system should start: with a plan.
